source.title: The German ZEW Indicator of Economic Sentiment Stands at plus 34.7 Points

evidence.dominant_driver: German ZEW expectations missed consensus while current conditions improved; high energy costs remain the larger European headwind.

market_expectations.distribution_notes: Consensus expected a materially stronger rise than delivered.

absorption.reason: European equities were already weak from oil/inflation/yield pressure before and around the release; ZEW adds only incremental downside information.

observed_reaction.GDAXI: already under pressure; no clean standalone ZEW break isolated

observations.European_equities: already lower, but current-situation component improved materially

evidence.decision_notes: Residual-move forecast from decision time; do not treat the consensus miss as a fresh large shock. No ACTIONABLE model-2 learning segment was used to alter confidence.

US2Y.source: no sufficiently fresh verified level found

immediate.rationale: Consensus miss is negative, but the release is partly absorbed and current conditions improved.

next_session.rationale: Fed/energy developments are likely to dominate the next session.

1h.rationale: Weak expectations plus expensive energy can keep pressure on German cyclicals.

next_session.rationale: Fed/energy developments are likely to dominate the next session.

predictions.mechanism: ZEW expectations miss reduces growth optimism, but improved current conditions and pre-existing oil/rates risk limit incremental signal.
predictions.counter_case: A fall in oil/yields or a relief bid in European cyclicals could overwhelm the modest ZEW miss.
